forecast-period.text: A low pressure system is entering the state from the west today, moving over central and eastern districts on Monday, followed by another ridge of high pressure which will persist until Tuesday. On Wednesday a cold front moves over the south of the state.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Possible morning fog patches about the southern agricultural area. Showers and possible thunderstorms developing about the agricultural area and south of the pastoral districts. Maximum temperatures above average in the west, grading to below average in the southeast. Light and variable winds about the eastern border, tending northeasterly. Elsewhere, north to northeasterly winds, fresh about the west ahead of a west to southwesterly change reaching central districts in the late evening.

Showers and possible thunderstorms about about central and eastern districts, contracting east during the day. Maximum temperatures near to above average. Fresh northeast to northwesterly winds about the east at first, tending fresh south to southwesterly about the west and extending throughout during the day.

Possible morning fog patches about central districts. Light showers about southern coasts. Possible morning thunderstorm about the far northeast. Maximum temperatures near to below average grading to above average in the west. Southeast to southwesterly winds.

text.p: Showers extending across the agricultural areas, with possible thunderstorms about the southern agricultural area. Maximum temperatures below average apart from in the northeast with maxima remaining above average. Light winds tending northwesterly ahead of a fresh and gusty southwesterly change extending throughout the day.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Wednesday: 1 to 5 mm about the northern agricultural area and south of the pastoral districts, increasing to 5 to 15 mm across the southern agricultural area, with possible falls of 15 to 30 mm about southern ranges and the Lower South East district. Higher totals of 30 to 50 mm possible with thunderstorms. Less than 2 mm about the far northeast.
